PRIVACY.TITLE: Privacy and Data Confidentiality Policy of MyMasterBook.net
PRIVACY.INTRO_P1: At MasterBook, we understand the importance of privacy and personal data protection. This Privacy and Confidentiality Policy (the "Policy") describes how MasterBook ("We", "Our" or "the Company") collects, uses, discloses, and protects the information that You ("User" or "You") provide to us when using our software as a service (SaaS) for insurance brokers (the "Service").
PRIVACY.INTRO_P2: By using the Service, You agree to the practices described in this Policy. If you do not agree with this Policy, you must not use the Service.

S1.TITLE: 1. Key Definitions
S1.T1: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ("Data Subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person.
S1.T2: Any operation or set of operations performed on Personal Data or sets of Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organization, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction.
S1.T3: The natural or legal person, public authority, agency, or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of Personal Data. In the context of your client and policy information that You upload to our Service, You are the Data Controller.
S1.T4: The natural or legal person, public authority, agency, or other body which processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller. In the context of your client and policy information that You upload to our Service, MasterBook is the Data Processor.
S1.T5: The natural or legal person who registers for and uses the Service, i.e., the insurance broker or insurance agency.

S2.TITLE: 2. Information We Collect
S2.INTRO: We collect two main types of information:
S2.SUB21: 2.1. Information You Provide Directly (User Account and Usage Data):
S2.T1: When you register for an account, we collect information such as your name, company name, email address, phone number, mailing address, billing information (e.g., credit card or bank account details), and login credentials.
S2.T2: Information you provide to us when you contact our technical support, sales, or any other inquiry (e.g., emails, chat transcripts).
S2.T3: Information you provide when you participate in surveys or provide us with feedback about the Service.
S2.SUB22: 2.2. Information We Collect Automatically (Usage and Technology Data):
S2.T4: Information about how you access and use the Service, including IP addresses, browser type, operating system, pages visited, time spent on the Service, clicks, and navigation paths.
S2.T5: We use cookies and similar tracking technologies (e.g., web beacons, pixels) to collect information about your browsing activity, personalize your experience, and perform analytics. You can manage your cookie preferences through your browser settings.
S2.SUB23: 2.3. User Content (Data Processed by Us on Your Behalf):
S2.T6: This is the most sensitive and crucial type of information. It comprises all the data that You (the User/Data Controller) upload, enter, or process through our Service, which may include, but is not limited to:
S2.L6: Personal Data of Your Clients and Potential Clients:
S2.T6_LIST: Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, dates of birth, health information (if relevant to the type of insurance), financial information, policy numbers, claims history, etc.
S2.T7_LIST: Insurance policy details, premiums, expiration dates, coverage information, claims data, and other operational data relevant to your insurance brokerage business.
S2.FOOTER: In relation to User Content, MasterBook acts strictly as a Data Processor, and You (the User) are the Data Controller. We do not use this User Content for our own purposes, except to provide and maintain the Service, prevent fraud, resolve technical issues, or as required by law.

S3.TITLE: 3. How We Use Information
S3.INTRO: We use the information collected for the following purposes:
S3.SUB31: 3.1. To Provide and Maintain the Service:
S3.I31_1: To operate, maintain, and improve the features and functionalities of the Service.
S3.I31_2: To manage your account and provide you with access to the Service.
S3.I31_3: To process your transactions and send you invoices and notices.
S3.I32_1: To respond to your technical support inquiries.
S3.I32_2: To send you service notifications, updates, security alerts, and administrative messages.
S3.I32_3: To send you marketing and promotional communications (with your consent, if required).
S3.SUB33: 3.3. To Improve and Personalize the Service:
S3.I33_1: To understand how users interact with the Service and develop new features.
S3.I33_2: To personalize your experience within the Service.
S3.I34_1: To detect and prevent fraudulent or unauthorized activities.

S4.TITLE: 4. How We Share Information
S4.INTRO: We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. We share information only in the following circumstances and for the purposes described in this Policy:
S4.T1: We share information with trusted service providers who perform functions on our behalf, such as payment processing, data hosting, data analysis, marketing, and customer support. These third parties are contractually obligated to protect the confidentiality and security of your information and to use it only for the purposes for which it has been provided.
S4.T2: We may share your information with our affiliated companies and subsidiaries to operate and improve our services.
S4.T3: In the event of a merger, acquisition, asset sale, or any other business transaction involving MasterBook, your information may be transferred as part of that transaction. We will notify you before your personal information is transferred and becomes subject to a different privacy policy.
S4.T4: We may disclose your information if we believe in good faith that it is necessary to: (a) comply with a legal obligation, such as a subpoena or court order; (b) protect and defend the rights or property of MasterBook; (c) prevent or investigate possible wrongdoing in connection with the Service; (d) protect the personal safety of Service users or the public; or (e) protect against legal liability.
S4.T5: We may share your information with third parties when we have your explicit consent to do so.

S5.TITLE: 5. User Content Data Protection (Data Processor Role)
S5.INTRO: As a Data Processor, we are committed to implementing appropriate technical and organizational security measures to protect User Content (which may include Personal Data of your clients) against unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. These measures include:
S5.T1: Encryption in transit and at rest, robust access controls, regular security audits, malware protection, and intrusion detection systems.
S5.T2: Internal data access policies, staff training on data protection, and confidentiality agreements with employees and contractors.
S5.T3: To comply with GDPR, CCPA, and other data protection laws, we offer a standard Data Processing Agreement (DPA) that governs our obligations as a Data Processor and your responsibilities as a Data Controller. You will be urged to sign this DPA if your operations require it.
S5.FOOTER: You, as the Data Controller, are responsible for:
S5.I1: Obtaining necessary consents from your clients to collect and process their Personal Data through the Service.
S5.I2: Ensuring that the User Content you upload to the Service is accurate, complete, and legal.
S5.I3: Responding to requests from Data Subjects (e.g., requests for access, rectification, erasure).

S6.TITLE: 6. International Data Transfers
S6.P1: Given the global nature of our Service, information may be transferred, stored, and processed in countries outside of your jurisdiction, including [e.g., United States, European Economic Area countries]. We will implement appropriate security measures to protect your personal information in accordance with this Policy and applicable law.
S6.T1: If we transfer Personal Data outside the European Economic Area (EEA) or the United Kingdom, we will rely on valid data transfer mechanisms, such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (if we are certified participants and transferring data to the U.S.), or binding corporate rules. You may request a copy of these mechanisms by contacting us.

S7.TITLE: 7. Your Privacy Rights
S7.INTRO: Depending on your location and applicable laws, you may have the following rights regarding your Personal Data:
S7.T1: The right to request a copy of the Personal Data we hold about you.
S7.T2: The right to request the correction of inaccurate or incomplete Personal Data.
S7.L3: Right to Erasure ("Right to be Forgotten"):
S7.T3: The right to request the deletion of your Personal Data under certain conditions.
S7.T4: The right to request the limitation of the processing of your Personal Data under certain conditions.
S7.T5: The right to receive your Personal Data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format, and to transmit it to another controller.
S7.T6: The right to object to the processing of your Personal Data under certain conditions (e.g., for direct marketing).
S7.T7: The right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affects you.
S7.T8: If processing is based on your consent, you have the right to withdraw it at any time. Withdrawal of consent will not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.
S7.FOOTER: To exercise any of these rights, please contact us using the information provided in Section 11. We may require you to verify your identity before processing your request.

S8.TITLE: 8. Data Retention
S8.P1: We will retain your Personal Data only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected, including for the purposes of satisfying any legal, accounting, or reporting requirements. The retention period for User Content (your clients' data) will depend on your instructions as the Data Controller, subject to our legal obligations as a Data Processor.

S9.TITLE: 9. Data Security
S9.P1: We have implemented commercially reasonable technical and organizational security measures designed to protect your Personal Data from unauthorized access, use, alteration, and disclosure. However, no data transmission over the Internet or storage system can be guaranteed to be 100% secure. Therefore, we cannot guarantee the absolute security of your information.

S10.TITLE: 10. Changes to this Privacy Policy
S10.P1: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any material changes by posting the revised Policy on our website or through direct notice.
